record.question: Which diseases are associated with BRCA1 and BRCA2?
prose_kept: The diseases associated with BRCA1 are Familial cancer of breast [1], Familial breast-ovarian cancer susceptibility 1 [2], Pancreatic cancer susceptibility 4 [3], and Fanconi anemia complementation group S [4].

The diseases associated with BRCA2 are Medulloblastoma [5], Fanconi anemia complementation group D1 [6], Familial breast-ovarian cancer susceptibility 2 [7], Glioma susceptibility 3 [8], Familial prostate cancer [9], Pancreatic cancer susceptibility 2 [10], and Wilms tumor 1 [11].
Mutations in this gene are responsible for approximately 40% of inherited breast cancers and more than 80% of inherited breast and ovarian cancers [12].

llm.reply:
The gene NCBIGene:672 (BRCA1) is associated with five hereditary cancer and anemia conditions: Familial cancer of breast, Familial breast-ovarian cancer susceptibility 1, Pancreatic cancer susceptibility 4, and Fanconi anemia complementation group S [1][2][3][4][5]. The gene NCBIGene:675 (BRCA2) is associated with seven conditions: Medulloblastoma, Fanconi anemia complementation group D1, Familial breast-ovarian cancer susceptibility 2, Glioma susceptibility 3, Familial prostate cancer, Pancreatic cancer susceptibility 2, and Wilms tumor 1 [6][7][8][9][10][11][12][13]. Both genes share susceptibility to breast-ovarian cancer and pancreatic cancer susceptibility, though each maps to distinct subtypes of these conditions.

## Hereditary Cancer Syndromes

BRCA1 and BRCA2 each confer susceptibility to site-specific familial breast-ovarian cancer through distinct genetic mechanisms: BRCA1 via Familial breast-ovarian cancer susceptibility 1 [3] and BRCA2 via Familial breast-ovarian cancer susceptibility 2 [9]. Additionally, BRCA2 carries risk for Familial prostate cancer [11], while BRCA1 is specifically linked to Familial cancer of breast [2].

## DNA Repair Dysfunction

Both genes participate in Fanconi anemia pathways through distinct complementation groups: BRCA1 as FANCS and BRCA2 as FANCD1 [5][8]. These associations reflect their shared function in homologous recombination repair of DNA double-strand breaks [21], with loss-of-function mutations producing chromosome instability syndromes.

## Additional Malignancy Risks

Beyond the core hereditary breast-ovarian cancer spectrum, each gene carries distinct tumor associations: BRCA1 with Pancreatic cancer susceptibility 4 [4], and BRCA2 with Pancreatic cancer susceptibility 2 [12], Medulloblastoma [7], Glioma susceptibility 3 [10], and Wilms tumor 1 [13]. The 190 kD nuclear phosphoprotein encoded by BRCA1 combines with DNA damage sensors and signal transducers to maintain genomic stability, with mutations responsible for approximately 40% of inherited breast cancers and more than 80% of inherited breast and ovarian cancers [24: "This gene encodes a 190 kD nuclear phosphoprotein...Mutations in this gene are responsible for approximately 40% of inherited breast cancers and more than 80% of inherited breast and ovarian cancers"].

The diseases associated with BRCA1 are Familial cancer of breast [2], Familial breast-ovarian cancer susceptibility 1 [3], Pancreatic cancer susceptibility 4 [4], and Fanconi anemia complementation group S [5]. The diseases associated with BRCA2 are Medulloblastoma [7], Fanconi anemia complementation group D1 [8], Familial breast-ovarian cancer susceptibility 2 [9], Glioma susceptibility 3 [10], Familial prostate cancer [11], Pancreatic cancer susceptibility 2 [12], and Wilms tumor 1 [13].

## BRCA1 Cancer Spectrum

BRCA1 is strongly linked to hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndromes. Mutations in this gene are responsible for approximately 40% of inherited breast cancers and more than 80% of inherited breast and ovarian cancers [24: "Mutations in this gene are responsible for approximately 40% of inherited breast cancers and more than 80% of inherited breast and ovarian cancers"]. The gene also confers susceptibility to pancreatic cancer through Pancreatic cancer susceptibility 4 [4] and to Fanconi anemia complementation group S [5], reflecting its core role in DNA repair [27].

## BRCA2 Cancer Spectrum

BRCA2 shows broader tumor associations beyond breast and ovarian malignancies. It is linked to Familial breast-ovarian cancer susceptibility 2 [9], Familial prostate cancer [11], and Pancreatic cancer susceptibility 2 [12], as well as to central nervous system tumors including Medulloblastoma [7] and Glioma susceptibility 3 [10]. BRCA2 also causes Fanconi anemia complementation group D1 [8], paralleling BRCA1's DNA repair function.

## Molecular and Clinical Context

Both genes encode DNA repair-associated proteins [1][6] and participate in double-strand break repair via homologous recombination [21]. Clinical investigation of BRCA1 includes trials examining haploinsufficiency and gene expression [25] and treatment customization in advanced lung carcinoma [30], while population-specific studies address germline mutations in Jewish women affected by breast cancer [19].
